subject: Post-call: Nimbus - scope for side-by-side tests vs hyperscalers
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Kevin Rios <kevin@nimbus-analytics.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: Nimbus - scope for side-by-side tests vs hyperscalers

Hi Kevin — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed scope for the side-by-side so we can keep procurement and engineering aligned: 

Summary of ask (from your team):
- Validate parity and quality vs your current hyperscaler endpoints for the three main flows: tool/function calling, structured JSON outputs, and streaming/long-answer latency.
- Proof points on tail latency and 95th pct for streaming sessions at both short (<=512 token) and long (2048+ token) sequences.
- A small set of representative prompts + expected JSON schema to check deterministic structure.
- Compliance checklist (SOC2 evidence, KMS support, private deployment options) for procurement.

Proposed Redwood deliverables:
1) Side-by-side test results spreadsheet (attached): we will run the same prompt set against Redwood hosted endpoint, an AWS Bedrock baseline (you mentioned Bedrock), and a Vertex/other baseline if you can provide access or a recording of their outputs.
2) Focused function-calling experiment: we will execute the provided "order_flow" sample and verify that our tool-calling hooks produce identical call name + args shape and deterministic fallbacks.
3) Structured output validation: 10 prompts mapped to your JSON schema — we will score structural correctness (valid JSON, required fields present) and semantic accuracy.
4) Streaming latency sweep: tests at 128/512/2048 token windows to measure first-byte latency and aggregate token throughput.
5) Compliance pack: high-level SOC2 artifact checklist and KMS overview (no customer data will be stored during these tests).

Timeline: we can start as soon as we receive your sample prompts + an indication of which hyperscaler endpoints you want us to include. Target: initial results by Tue Nov 10, 2026.

Attachments: redwood-nimbus-test-scope.xlsx (test matrix + scoring), nimbus-sample-prompts.jsonl (please confirm this is the canonical set).

Next steps / asks for you:
- Share the accepted sample prompts (or confirm the attached file).
- Tell us which hyperscaler endpoints you want included (Bedrock, Vertex, other) and whether you can share access or recorded outputs.
- Procurement contact (who should we send SOC2 checklist to?).

I’ll loop Sean and Marissa into the test orchestration; we’ll keep the report focused on actionable parity gaps and recommended mitigations.

Thanks — talk soon.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0191

From: Kevin Rios <kevin@nimbus-analytics.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Nimbus - scope for side-by-side tests vs hyperscalers

Vanessa — appreciate the clear plan and the spreadsheet. Quick answers from our side: 

- Confirm attached prompt set (I also uploaded a slightly updated prompts.jsonl to your Drive link).
- Please include Bedrock (the main baseline) and Vertex if possible. We cannot share direct credentials to Bedrock, but I can export a small sample of their outputs for the same prompts (CSV) by EOD Thu.
- Procurement contact: Priya Mathews (priya.mathews@nimbus-analytics.com). She will want SOC2 + KMS details and a short statement about data retention during testing.
- A key question: for the function-calling test we need to see whether Redwood preserves named argument order and explicitly returns call metadata (call_name, confidence, raw_args) in the same shape as Bedrock. If there is a shaping step required on our side, tell us now.

I attached the first batch of Bedrock outputs (bedrock_sample_outputs.csv) so you can start. We’re also looking at failure modes — e.g., how often each platform returns unparsable JSON and how graceful the fallback is.

Can we do a quick checkpoint on Mon Nov 9 (30 min) to review initial findings? Thanks.

— Kevin
Lead ML Engineer, Nimbus Analytics
kevin@nimbus-analytics.com

On Tue, Nov 3, 2026 at 3:12 PM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Kevin — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed scope for the side-by-side so we can keep procurement and engineering aligned: ...

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 11:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: test ownership and runbook for Nimbus side-by-side

Team — quick internal coordination. Kevin sent the Bedrock sample outputs this morning (CCed). Proposed split of work: 

- Marissa: own structured-output scoring (schema validation, field-level precision/recall). Use the scoring tabs in redwood-nimbus-test-scope.xlsx. Please produce a reproducible evaluation notebook and the seed list for generation.
- Vanessa: coordinator and external liaison — you’ll confirm timeline and send SOC2 checklist to Priya.
- Sean (me): run the streaming latency sweep across our hosted and dedicated endpoints (128/512/2048) and capture first-byte and token throughput. I’ll also check the KV cache behavior with repeated prefixes to match their production pattern.

Notes / implementation details: 
- For function-calling parity, we should return a consistent object: {call_name, call_args, confidence, raw_model_output}. We will include an optional 'reconstructed_args' field when we perform sanitization/normalization. Call out any cases where our normalization would change argument order or key names.
- For determinism checks: run 5 seeds per prompt with identical temperature/beam settings and report variance in returned JSON shape and semantic fields.

I’ll stand up the test cluster today; target to run the initial pass by EOD Nov 9 so we can present on Nov 10 if Kevin confirms.

— Sean
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Kevin Rios <kevin@nimbus-analytics.com>, Priya Mathews <priya.mathews@nimbus-analytics.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Nimbus - scope for side-by-side tests vs hyperscalers — next steps and meeting

Kevin / Priya — thanks for the quick replies and for sharing the Bedrock sample. Short summary of confirmed plan and asks: 

Confirmed scope: 
- Function-calling parity test (order_flow sample) — Redwood will return call_name + call_args + confidence + raw_model_output. We will include both native args and a normalized 'reconstructed_args' when we sanitize.
- Structured JSON outputs — 10 canonical prompts mapped to your schema; we will report parse success rate and per-field accuracy.
- Streaming latency sweep — first-byte and throughput at 128 / 512 / 2048 tokens.
- Compliance checklist to Priya: SOC2 artifact list, KMS integrations, retention policy (we will not persist customer prompt data beyond the test window unless authorized).

Deliverables & timeline: 
- Initial results (spreadsheet + short slide summary): by Tue Nov 10, 2026.
- Checkpoint call: Mon Nov 9, 30 minutes — Vanessa, Sean, Marissa + Kevin (Priya optional). Please indicate preferred time window; we propose 10:00–11:00 PT.

Attachments we’ve pushed to the shared Drive: redwood-nimbus-test-scope.xlsx, nimbus-sample-prompts.jsonl. We'll add the runbook and the evaluation notebook after the initial pass.

Kevin — can you confirm access to the Bedrock outputs for the full prompt list by Thu Nov 5 so we can include direct comparisons? If not, the CSV exports you shared will be sufficient for an initial pass but may limit per-token latency comparisons.

Thanks — looking forward to the run.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0191
